counterfactual_missing_items: No evidence of iron deficiency (ferritin elevated, iron studies normal)
No hypertensive retinopathy pattern (optic cupping is not typical)
No alternative cause for anemia other than chronic disease
decisive_items: diffuse intimal thickening with narrowing at the origins of the brachiocephalic, right common carotid, and left subclavian arteries
a bruit was audible over the left subclavian fossa
pulses in both upper limbs were deficient and blood pressure could not be measured
response.rationale: R3 uniquely matches the full clinical picture: young female with absent upper-limb pulses, subclavian bruit, and CTA showing large-vessel stenosis with collaterals, plus elevated inflammatory markers. R2 explains only the anemia but misses the vascular findings. R1 is contradicted by elevated ferritin and normal iron studies. R4 lacks specific retinal changes. C1 is a subtype of R2 and not a separate diagnosis.

rejected.why: Iron deficiency is contradicted by elevated ferritin and normal iron studies; microcytic anemia is better explained by chronic disease.
Optic-disk cupping is not characteristic of hypertensive retinopathy; no other hypertensive stigmata and blood pressure was unmeasurable.
Append-only completion of R2, not an independent diagnosis; does not address the vascular syndrome.
